newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU must move towards more majority voting - Dini.
newsitem.headline: EU must move towards more majority voting - Dini.

text.p: The European Union must reform its decision-making process to incorporate greater majority voting or suffer serious setbacks ahead of eastern enlargement, Italian foreign minister Lamberto Dini said on Wednesday.
Speaking to a committee of the European Parliament, Dini argued forcefully for less reliance on unanimity, the current voting procedure on a wide range of EU policy issues.
"We believe the European Union wouldn't work without a move to majority voting," Dini said.
He acknowledged, however, that Italy was in a minority on this issue in current negotiations to reform the Maastricht Treaty.

EU foreign ministers, meeting in The Hague on Tuesday, were more optimistic on agreeing landmark treaty reforms at an Amsterdam summit in four weeks after narrowing their differences on several key issues.
Taking a less upbeat view of Tuesday's gathering, Dini said several EU governments were more concerned about the substance of negotiations than with meeting a specific deadline.
"There are a certain number of countries which believe we must put substance before the timetable," he said.
"If we are not satisfied on these principles, we and others have said we would not be prepared to sign the treaty."

EU heads of state and government are due to meet in the Dutch coastal town of Noordwijk on Friday for a half-day informal session to gauge the chances of a successful outcome to an 18-month inter-governmental conference (IGC) treaty review, due to be completed in Amsterdam on June 16-17.
Dini also said he would not put a revised EU treaty before the Italian parliament for approval until the European Parliament had had a chance to give its own opinion.
On other issues, the Italian minister said he favoured giving the EU a "legal personality" who would represent the 15-nation bloc in international forums.
